title: How do you give a strong recommendation at the end of a case?
description: The last 60 seconds are what the interviewer remembers. Answer first, reasons with numbers, risks, next steps.
hook: The end of a case is where many good candidates lose marks, because they are tired and summarise everything they did instead of answering the question. A strong recommendation is short: the answer first, then the reasons, the risks and the next steps. This guide shows you exactly how to say it.
body:
In this guide

  • Answer first
  • The structure: answer, reasons, risks, next steps
  • A worked example
  • What to remember
  • Check yourself

Answer first

Open with the recommendation itself: "I recommend entering the US through a distributor." Not "So, first we looked at the market..." The interviewer has just watched the whole case and doesn't need a replay.

The structure: answer, reasons, risks, next steps

  • Answer: one sentence.
  • Two or three reasons, each with a number from the case.
  • The main risk, and how you'd manage it.
  • Next steps, including any branch of your structure you didn't get to.

Take 20 seconds to prepare ("May I take a moment to put this together?"), then speak for about 60. Talk to the interviewer as if they were the client's CEO.

See it in action: A 60-second recommendation

"I recommend PackRight buys RePlast, but not at a flat $180M. Two reasons: recycled plastic becomes scarce from 2028, and RePlast covers two-thirds of what PackRight legally needs by 2030. With all synergies it's worth about $215M to us, but without the uncertain green premium only $155M. So I'd offer around $160M plus an earn-out tied to signed premium contracts. The key risk is food-grade quality, so next steps are technical due diligence and talks with three anchor customers."

What to remember

  • Start with the answer.
  • Each reason gets a number from the case.
  • Risks and next steps show you see the whole picture.

Check yourself

Have a go at each one before you open the answer.

1. How should a recommendation begin?

  • With a summary of the case
  • With the recommendation itself
  • By thanking the interviewer
Show the answer

With the recommendation itself. Answer first. Reasons follow.

2. Where do unexplored parts of your structure belong?

  • Nowhere: don’t mention them
  • In next steps
  • At the start of the recommendation
Show the answer

In next steps. Naming them as next steps shows you tracked the whole problem.

Try it now

You found: the bakery chain’s target cities are growing 8% a year; a new site pays back its investment in about 2 years; but opening five cities at once would mean moving three of your best managers. Give a 60-second recommendation out loud.

Give yourself 60 seconds, out loud if you can.

Show a strong answer

"I recommend expanding, but in two phases rather than all five cities at once. The market grows 8% a year and a site pays back in about two years, so the opportunity is real. The main risk is management: moving three top managers could hurt existing shops. So start with two cities, hire and train managers in parallel, and open the other three once those sites hit their numbers."

Reconcile your recommendation with the client's target

Assume the client needs £5 million of additional annual profit. Your analysis finds two credible initiatives: £2 million from procurement savings and £1.5 million from reducing returns. An answer that claims the target is solved is wrong: the quantified gap is still £1.5 million.

A strong recommendation makes that visible: implement the two supported levers, validate savings through pilots, and investigate one additional lever or revise the target if the remaining gap cannot be closed responsibly. Flag implementation costs and risks separately from recurring benefits.

Use plain language rather than a rehearsed closing formula. Executives need to know the decision, the evidence, what could overturn it and the next step. The exact ordering of risk and implementation details matters less than answering the question they asked.
